headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, MCP-enabled workspace can leak sensitive travel data and create cascading action errors when paired with Rasa’s chat-driven outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Rasa ingests conversational text and can surface it through messaging channels, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with MCP and browser access. That creates a plausible path where TREK content is treated as instructions by Rasa or vice versa, especially through shared chat-like surfaces. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF TREK content is forwarded into Rasa’s dialogue pipeline without provenance tagging
IF either agent parses the other’s text as executable instructions
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all cross-agent messages
Strip tool directives from shared text before ingestion
Route inter-agent traffic through a fixed schema
Disable MCP bridges for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Rasa handles text/voice and has allowlisted network egress. If TREK data is passed into Rasa for conversation handling, sensitive travel and account data can leave the local workspace through outbound APIs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default docs, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK passes reservations, documents, or secrets into Rasa prompts or logs
IF Rasa forwards those contents to external messaging APIs or allowlisted egress destinations
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff
Keep TREK sensitive files out of Rasa inputs
Disable logging of message payloads
Restrict Rasa egress destinations to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and conversational workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa has allowlisted network egress and TREK supports browser, MCP, WebSocket, and shared files, so both can mutate or read overlapping external resources if orchestrated together. TREK is explicitly collaborative and supports multiple instances, while Rasa does not support multiple instances, increasing coordination risk. The overlap is real but not enough to prove same-dir filesystem contention, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external account or API scope
IF the orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent edits on shared resources
Use per-agent work queues
requires-engineering: add resource locks for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa produces conversational outputs that TREK can plausibly consume in a collaborative planning flow, and TREK handles reservations, budgets, and confirmation numbers. If TREK treats Rasa’s output as authoritative, a mistaken itinerary or booking instruction can cascade into user-visible or externally executed actions. Because TREK has action-bearing surfaces and the verification step is not documented, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK uses Rasa-generated text as booking or planning authority
IF no human or rule-based verification occurs before reservations or account actions
mitigations: Require human approval before bookings
Add validation against source data
Show confidence and provenance on all handoffs
Block direct execution from free-text outputs
requires-engineering: implement structured action schemas

E_compliance.rationale: TREK touches email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, MFA secrets, and country visit history, while Rasa handles conversational text and voice with outbound API access. If regulated or sensitive travel/account data flows from TREK into Rasa’s external channels, retention and residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so uncertainty should be resolved upward.
conditions: IF personal travel records or account secrets are routed from TREK into Rasa-hosted services
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Minimize shared personal data
Document retention for both systems
Pseudonymize identifiers before transfer
Restrict exports to approved jurisdictions
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPAs
